advances: Conditional mixed-area bound for actual covers with locally bisected planar chords and stated balance. General cap-group selection does not supply these hypotheses.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Fix a triple and an owned fiber. The proper chord has its relative midpoint in the interior of the body. Indeed its line meets the interior, and convex combinations of an interior point on the line with the endpoints give all relative interior chord points in the body interior. Translate the common midpoint to the origin and write $R$ for the positive quarter-turn. The endpoints of the $i$-th chord are $\pm p_i$ with $Rp_i=s_{ji}(z)u_{ji}/2$. These are boundary points of the actual fiber, and the closed cap is exactly the inward halfplane prescribed by $Rp_i$. The definition of $\theta_j(z)$ gives $\sum_i\theta_{ji}(z)p_i=0$. The accepted bisected-chord theorem b82858197fd14145 on this planar body, with precisely these probabilities and its original area, gives $\sum_i\theta_{ji}(z)p_{ji}(z)\ge4/9$.

The difference vector $\theta_j-\theta_j(z)$ has sum zero and its negative part has mass $\tfrac12\sum_i|\theta_{ji}-\theta_{ji}(z)|$. Subtracting $\min_i p_{ji}(z)$ from each coordinate of the vector of cap fractions shows that the change in the weighted fraction is at least $-r_j(z)\tfrac12\sum_i|\theta_{ji}-\theta_{ji}(z)|$. Multiply by $w_z$ and sum over $P_j$. The exact contribution of the nonowned fibers to the global weighted cap sum is $X_j$. Each global cap mass is at most $B$, so their probability-weighted sum is at most $B$. These steps give the first inequality. For one or two caps the union bound gives the stated inequalities without chord hypotheses. Summation uses $\sum_j W_j=M$.

The difference $X_j-E_j$ is continuous on the compact probability simplex. To express its maximum as a linear program, put a nonnegative slack above both signs of each $\theta_{ji}-\theta_{ji}(z)$, and subtract that slack with coefficient $w_zr_j(z)/2$ in the linear objective. For every fixed $\theta_j$ choosing the absolute values realizes $X_j-E_j$, and increasing a slack cannot raise the objective. Finally, proportional lengths cancel the common $a_z$ from the balancing vector, giving $E_j=0$ and the stated bound since $X_j\ge0$.

statement:
Let finitely many positive planar convex integer fibers $K_z$ of areas $w_z$ have total mixed area $M$. Assign their bases to disjoint sets $P_1,\dots,P_k$, one for each group of one, two, or three original closed ambient caps, whose traces cover the group's owned fibers. Every cap has global mixed mass at most $B$, where $\mu$ denotes summed fiber area. Write $S_j$ for the union of the owned fibers of group $j$ in the mixed set $S$, and $W_j=\mu(S_j)$.

For each triple group require that its continuous inward unit normals $u_{ji}$ form a minimal positive dependence $\sum_i\rho_{ji}u_{ji}=0$ with $\rho_{ji}>0$. On each owned fiber require proper chords with a common midpoint. Write $s_{ji}(z)$ for the chord lengths and set
$$
\theta_{ji}(z)=\frac{\rho_{ji}/s_{ji}(z)}{\sum_l\rho_{jl}/s_{jl}(z)},\quad
p_{ji}(z)=\frac{|K_z\cap H_{ji}(z)|}{w_z},\quad
r_j(z)=\max_i p_{ji}(z)-\min_i p_{ji}(z).
$$
For any probability vector $\theta_j$ independent of the owned base define
$$
E_j=\sum_{z\in P_j}w_zr_j(z)\,\frac12\sum_i|\theta_{ji}-\theta_{ji}(z)|,\qquad
X_j=\sum_i\theta_{ji}\mu(H_{ji}\cap(S\setminus S_j)).
$$
Then $B\ge(4/9)W_j-E_j+X_j$. For a one- or two-cap group the respective estimates are $B\ge W_j$ and $B\ge W_j/2$, and set $E_j=X_j=0$ for those groups in the sum. Consequently
$$
kB\ge\frac49M+\sum_j(X_j-E_j).
$$
For each triple the maximum of $X_j-E_j$ over $\theta_j$ is attained and is the value of a finite linear program. If in each triple the chord lengths factor as $s_{ji}(z)=a_z s_{ji}$ with $a_z,s_{ji}>0$, one common vector $\theta_{ji}=(\rho_{ji}/s_{ji})/\sum_l(\rho_{jl}/s_{jl})$ gives $E_j=0$. In this case $kB\ge(4/9)M$ and $k\le2^n$ implies $B\ge (4/9)M/2^n$.
title: Weighted cross-capture and chord dispersion for planar cap groups
